questions.stem: A major feature of the presidential system of government is that

options.text: the President is both Head of State and Head of Government
the Prime Minister is answerable to parliament
ministers must be serving members of the legislature
the executive can be removed by a vote of no confidence

questions.explanation: In a presidential system the ceremonial and executive functions are combined in one directly elected office. That is why there is no separate Prime Minister in Nigeria or the United States.

distractorRationale.b: A Prime Minister answerable to parliament belongs to the parliamentary system
distractorRationale.c: In a presidential system ministers are barred from sitting in the legislature
distractorRationale.d: The vote of no confidence is a parliamentary device; a President is removed by impeachment

questions.stem: In a parliamentary system, a government that loses a vote of no confidence must

options.text: continue in office until its fixed term expires
resign or seek a dissolution of parliament
be tried before the highest court in the land
be dismissed by the ceremonial Head of State on his own initiative

questions.explanation: Because the executive holds office only while it commands the confidence of the legislature, losing that confidence ends its mandate. The convention is that the Prime Minister resigns or asks the Head of State to dissolve parliament for a fresh election.

distractorRationale.a: There is no fixed term protecting a parliamentary executive; that is a presidential feature
distractorRationale.c: Loss of confidence is a political judgement, not a criminal charge
distractorRationale.d: The ceremonial Head of State acts on advice, not on personal initiative

questions.stem: Nigeria's Head of Government between independence in 1960 and the coup of January 1966 was

options.text: Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe as President
Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa as Prime Minister
Chief Obafemi Awolowo as Premier
Sir Ahmadu Bello as Sardauna

questions.explanation: Nigeria operated a parliamentary system in the First Republic, so the Head of Government was the Prime Minister, Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa. Dr Azikiwe was Governor-General from 1960 and then ceremonial President from 1963.

distractorRationale.a: Azikiwe held the ceremonial headship of state, not the headship of government
distractorRationale.c: Awolowo was Premier of the Western Region and later federal opposition leader, not head of the federal government
distractorRationale.d: Ahmadu Bello was Premier of the Northern Region and chose to remain there rather than lead at the centre

questions.stem: The clearest single test for deciding whether a country operates a parliamentary system is whether

options.text: the country has a written constitution
ministers are also serving members of the legislature
the country holds elections every four years
the country is a member of the Commonwealth

questions.explanation: Overlapping personnel is the essence of fusion. If ministers sit and vote in the legislature the system is parliamentary; if they are barred from doing so, as section 147 of Nigeria's 1999 Constitution requires, the system is presidential.

distractorRationale.a: Both systems can operate with or without a written constitution; Britain is parliamentary with an unwritten one
distractorRationale.c: Election frequency varies within both systems and decides nothing
distractorRationale.d: Commonwealth membership includes both presidential Nigeria and parliamentary India

questions.stem: A frequently cited disadvantage of the presidential system is that

options.text: the executive can be removed too easily by the legislature
deadlock can arise when the President and the legislature disagree
ministers have no experience of legislative business
the tenure of the executive is too uncertain

questions.explanation: Because the two organs are separately elected, neither can compel the other. If the President's party does not control the legislature, budgets and appointments can stall, and there is no vote of no confidence to break the impasse.

distractorRationale.a: Removal is difficult under a presidential system, requiring impeachment for gross misconduct
distractorRationale.c: Ministers may lack legislative experience, but that is a minor criticism rather than the classic structural one
distractorRationale.d: Presidential tenure is fixed and therefore certain; uncertainty is the parliamentary weakness

questions.stem: The doctrine of collective responsibility, under which all ministers must publicly support cabinet decisions or resign, belongs to

options.text: the presidential system
the parliamentary system
military government
the confederal system

questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system the cabinet stands or falls together before the legislature, so it must present one face publicly. Under a presidential system ministers answer individually to the President who appointed them.

distractorRationale.a: Presidential ministers are individually accountable to the President, not collectively to a legislature
distractorRationale.c: Military regimes operate by command from a ruling council, not by cabinet convention
distractorRationale.d: Confederalism concerns the relationship between a centre and its component states

questions.stem: Nigeria adopted the presidential system of government for the first time under the 1979 Constitution.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. The 1960 Independence and 1963 Republican Constitutions both provided for a parliamentary system with a Prime Minister. The presidential model, with a directly elected President as Head of State and Head of Government, came in with the 1979 Constitution and was retained in 1999.

distractorRationale.b: This would imply an earlier presidential constitution, but Nigeria's 1963 President was a ceremonial one in a parliamentary system

questions.stem: Under Nigeria's 1999 Constitution, a President may be removed from office through

options.text: a simple majority vote of no confidence in the Senate
impeachment for gross misconduct following the constitutional procedure
a directive of the Chief Justice of Nigeria
dissolution of the National Assembly

questions.explanation: Impeachment is the only constitutional route, and it is deliberately demanding: an allegation of gross misconduct, investigation by a panel appointed by the Chief Justice, and a two-thirds resolution of each chamber. This protects the fixed tenure that defines the presidential system.

distractorRationale.a: The vote of no confidence exists in parliamentary systems and has no place in Nigeria's presidential arrangement
distractorRationale.c: The Chief Justice appoints the investigating panel but cannot remove a President
distractorRationale.d: The National Assembly cannot be dissolved to unseat a President; both have separate fixed terms

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), section 143
